title: Grateful Dead Live at Springer's Inn Portland on 1970-01-16
source: Source: sbd > reel master > reel > pcm (sony beta tape ESX-HiFi/L-750) - Given to Tim Dalton by the late Harvey Lubar; Transfer: pcm > Sony SL-10 > Sony PCM-601ESD > Behringer Ultramatch Pro > Tascam DA-3000 (WAV 16-bit/44.1k) - transferred by Charlie Miller; Lineage: wav > iZotope RX6 Advanced > iZotope 5 Advanced > CD Wave > TLH > Flac 16; edited and mastered SIRMick February 2018

ai_review.summary: Rough early‑70 soundboard capture of a primo Dead show featuring a standout China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider sequence.
ai_review.review: The recording is a raw, early‑70s soundboard tape that sounds a bit rough but remains listenable. The performance shines with Jerry digging into the new China > Rider jam, marking this period as “primo Dead.” One reviewer notes the absence of “Easy Wind,” which tempers the overall enthusiasm.

ai_rating.rationale: Show is praised for strong playing and a notable China > Rider sequence (70% weight), while recording quality is described as rough/typical of the era (30% weight). Mixed comments about missing material lower the overall score slightly.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Typical early‑70s raw sound; described as “rough” but no specific dropouts or balance issues noted. Overall listenable despite the vintage tape character.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: Early‑70s set is described as rough yet good, with a strong jam flow highlighted by the China > Rider sequence; overall energy reflects a prime Dead period.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Jerry is noted for digging into the new China > Rider thing and delivering strong guitar work.
